transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I can't ever just idle. And the new work setup has made that a lot harder to hide. 

They just moved all of us customer service reps to this new open-floor plan. Which, honestly, is a terrible idea. I mean, you've got fifty people all talking on headsets at once, and the headsets they gave us are those cheap foam ones? My ear actually gets a rash if I wear it for more than an hour. My wife told me to put a little baby powder on it, but that just gets all over my shirt collar, and then it looks like I've been eating powdered donuts all morning. I complained to HR about the headsets, but they said it's standard issue now. 

But anyway... yeah, I just can't idle, and with the new desks, everyone can see it now.
Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or irritable compared with your normal self?

Unusually high? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't get super high or anything. I get irritated, sure, but just the normal amount, you know? 

Like, when someone leaves the breakroom microwave covered in whatever they just heated up. Yesterday it looked like a literal tomato soup explosion in there. Who just leaves that? It’s a shared space. And don't even get me started on the coffee machine. Management switched us to this cheap brand to save a few bucks, and it tastes like burnt dirt. My wife tells me I should just bring a thermos from home, but by the time I get through the morning traffic on the interstate—which is a total nightmare right now because of that construction they're doing on the overpass—the coffee is lukewarm anyway. I even bought one of those fancy insulated travel mugs, but the seal on the lid is defective or something because it always leaks right onto my car seats. I tried to return it, but I didn't have the receipt... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, my mood. Yeah, no, just regular annoyed by stuff like that. Nothing out of the ordinary.
Before age 12, were you already the kind of person who had trouble sitting still or staying focused?

Yeah, looking back, this was around long before this job change. I mean, way back in grade school. I remember my mom used to keep all my report cards in this old shoebox. And every single year, the teachers wrote the exact same thing: that I was a bright kid but careless, that I talked out of turn too much, and they always had to remind me to stay with my work. 

My mom actually kept that shoebox in her basement for years, right up until the water heater busted back in '08. Total disaster. Ruined half our family photos and all those old school papers. We had to hire this guy, Gary, to come fix the plumbing, and he charged us an arm and a leg just to tell us the subfloor was rotted. You really can't trust contractors these days, they just look at you and see dollar signs. And Gary didn't even take off his muddy boots when he walked on the living room carpet. My wife spent three hours scrubbing clay out of the rug with club soda and vinegar. She swears by vinegar for everything, but honestly it just makes the house smell like a pickle factory for a week... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, right, being a kid. But yeah, the teachers were always having to remind me to just do my work.
Do you often feel physically restless, like you need to keep moving even when you’re supposed to stay seated?

Yeah, I do. Sitting still through a training video or, you know, a slow appointment, it makes me feel kind of boxed in. Like I just need to stand up, stretch, or do something with my hands. 

We had this mandatory training last week on the new software system they're rolling out. And let me tell you, this new software is a joke. It takes five clicks just to open a customer's profile, whereas the old system took two. I timed it. And the trainer they brought in? He just read off the PowerPoint slides in this total monotone voice. He was wearing this tie with little golf clubs on it, which I thought was kind of funny because my brother-in-law plays golf every weekend and he's terrible at it. Slices it into the woods every time. He actually lost a brand new sleeve of Pro V1s on the front nine last Sunday. Those aren't cheap, you know. I told him he should just buy the recycled ones from the sporting goods store, but he says they don't fly right. I don't know, a golf ball is a golf ball to me. I prefer bowling anyway. 

But yeah, I had to keep shifting around in my chair the whole training. I ended up taking apart my pen and putting it back together like ten times just to keep my hands busy.
Do you often have trouble sustaining your attention on tasks, even when you want to focus?

Oh, absolutely. Like, if I have to sit through one of those longer coaching meetings, or if I’m trying to read a new procedure, I really do want to focus. I'll start off fine, but after a few minutes, I’ll realize my eyes just kept moving down the page and I didn’t really take in a single thing that was said or written. 

It doesn't help that corporate started printing the new procedure updates on this weird glossy paper. I don't know whose bright idea that was, but the glare from the fluorescent lights in our office makes it terrible to look at. And speaking of the lights, the one right above my desk has been flickering for three weeks. I put in a ticket with Steve, the maintenance guy, but he's always just sitting out back by the loading dock scrolling on his phone. I swear, nobody looks up from their screens anymore. My nephew came over for dinner last Sunday and spent the entire meal watching videos under the table. My sister didn't even tell him to put it away! If I did that when I was his age, my dad would have sent me straight to my room without supper. We had pot roast, too, which is my favorite, though my wife always overcooks the carrots... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, paying attention. Yeah, I just stop absorbing whatever I'm supposed to be focusing on.
Do you often blurt things out or interrupt people before they’ve finished talking?

Yeah, I do that a lot actually. I don't mean to be rude or anything, but if I hear some of the younger coworkers in the next cubicle trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump right in with the answer before they're even finished explaining it to each other, or before anyone even asked for my help. 

The walls in our office are so thin, you know? They're those cheap fabric dividers that don't block out any sound at all. They used to be this nice gray color, but over the years they've faded to this weird, dusty beige. And people just pin the most random stuff to them. The guy next to me, Kevin, he has all these pictures of his cats pinned up. He's got like four cats, which seems excessive to me. I'm more of a dog person myself. We had a Golden Retriever named Buster when I was growing up. Best dog ever. He used to chase the mail truck down the street every single morning. The mailman, Mr. Henderson, he was a good sport about it. He always kept a box of milk bones in his truck for Buster. You don't see mailmen like that anymore. Now they just toss the packages on the porch and run. I had a package stolen right off my steps last month. It was a new pair of insoles for my work shoes, too. My arches have been killing me lately...

Anyway, yeah, I just blurt out the answer to the customer issues before they even finish talking.
Do you often act before thinking?

Act before thinking? I don't... I don't really think so. I mean, I try to think things through. Like when we bought our new car last year, I spent three weeks researching different models. We ended up getting a Honda CR-V because the gas mileage is pretty good and the trunk space is huge. We needed the space because my wife loves going to those antique fairs on the weekends. She collects these old ceramic pitchers. She must have, I don't know, forty of them by now. They're all over the house. Dusting them is a nightmare, let me tell you. I tried using one of those Swiffer dusters, but it just pushes the dust around, it doesn't really pick it up. I prefer the old-fashioned feather dusters, but you can't find a good one these days. The feathers always fall out after two uses. I bought one at the hardware store downtown—the one next to the old movie theater that shut down during the pandemic. It's a shame, they used to show classic movies on Tuesday nights. I saw Casablanca there on the big screen once. Humphrey Bogart, what a legend. 

But no, I don't really feel like I just act without thinking about it first.
Do you have the same trouble focusing at home, too?

At home? No, I haven't really noticed it there. I mean, when I'm home, I'm usually just relaxing or working out in the yard. I take a lot of pride in my lawn, actually. I use this special fertilizer I get from the garden center out on Route 9. The guy who runs it, Sal, he knows absolutely everything about soil pH. He told me the secret is to aerate in the fall, not the spring. My neighbor, Gary, he always does his in the spring and his grass looks terrible by July. Just full of these big brown patches. Gary's a good guy, though, he lent me his power washer last summer when I was trying to clean the vinyl siding. The siding gets so filthy from those big oak trees in our front yard. They drop these little stringy pollen things everywhere in May. My wife's allergies go absolutely crazy when they do. She has to buy the expensive tissues with the lotion in them, otherwise her nose gets all red and chapped... 

Wait, what did you ask me about being at home?
At home, do you also feel restless, like you need to keep moving or fidgeting?

Restless at home? No, I don't think so. I mean, usually when I get home from work I'm pretty beat, so I just want to sit down in my recliner. It's one of those La-Z-Boys, you know? Got it on sale at that furniture liquidator place that used to be a bowling alley. You can still see the lane markings on the floor if you look close enough. I used to bowl in a league back in the nineties. We were called the Pin Pals, real original, I know. Our team captain, Dave, he was a fanatic. He had this custom bowling ball that looked like a giant eyeball. It was the creepiest thing, watching it roll down the lane. Dave actually moved down to Florida a few years ago. Bought a condo in one of those retirement communities where everyone drives golf carts everywhere. I don't think I could do that. I like having a real car. The CR-V, like I was saying before, it's just so reliable. 

But yeah, I just sit in my chair and watch the news, I don't really feel like I need to be moving around or anything.
Outside of work, do you also tend to interrupt people before they’ve finished talking?

Outside of work? I don't know, maybe sometimes with my wife, but mostly I just notice it at the office. Like, I don't mean to be rude at all, but if I hear my coworkers working through a customer problem in the cubicle next to me, I'll just jump in with an answer before they've even finished talking or before anyone even asked me. It's just that I've been doing customer service for so long, I know the answers right away. 

We use this computer system at work that is so outdated, I swear it's from the Stone Age. They keep saying they're going to upgrade it, but the IT department had all these budget cuts last quarter. The head of IT, Frank, he's always complaining about the budget in the breakroom. He drives this immaculate vintage Mustang, cherry red. Must have cost him an absolute fortune to restore. I always see him parking it way out in the back of the lot so nobody dings the doors with their shopping carts. Well, not shopping carts, we don't have those at the office, but you know what I mean. People are so careless with their car doors. I used to have a Mustang back in my twenties, a '79. Man, I loved that car, but the transmission blew when I was driving up to the lake for a fishing trip. We used to go up to Lake Winnipesaukee every summer. The bass fishing up there is unbelievable if you know which coves to go to... 

Wait, what were we just talking about? Did you ask about my coworkers?
Outside of work, do you often feel like you have to keep moving?

Outside of work? No, I wouldn't say that. Like I said, I'm pretty content just kicking back in the La-Z-Boy. Although, my wife did get me this new pedometer thing for my birthday. She says I need to get my steps in. It's one of those fancy ones that syncs up to your phone and buzzes if you've been sitting too long. I don't really pay attention to the buzzing, honestly. The battery on my phone is always dying anyway. I think I need to get the charging port cleaned out. I tried using a toothpick the other day, but the tip broke off inside. Total disaster. I had to take it to one of those little repair kiosks in the mall. The kid working there looked like he was about twelve years old, but he had it fixed in two minutes flat. Charged me twenty bucks, though. Twenty bucks for two minutes of work! I should have gone into the electronics repair business instead of customer service. You know, my uncle used to fix TVs back when they were those huge wooden console things. He had a whole workshop in his basement... 

Sorry, did you ask if I feel like I have to keep moving? No, not really.
When you’re not at work, do you often interrupt people before they’ve finished speaking?

Well, outside of work, maybe a little bit with my wife, but I mostly just do it at the office. I really don't mean to be rude or anything, it's just... well, if I hear the guys in the cubicle next to me trying to figure out a customer issue, I'll just jump right in with the answer before they're even done talking. Or even if they didn't ask me. I just know the answers, you know? 

Speaking of the guys in the cubicles, they just rearranged our whole floor last month. Put me right next to the breakroom. You'd think that would be great, being close to the coffee maker, but the machine they have is this ancient drip thing that takes twenty minutes to brew a pot. And nobody ever makes a new pot when they take the last cup. It's a huge pet peeve of mine. My wife got us one of those Keurig machines for the house, the ones that take the little plastic pods? It's so fast, but I feel kind of bad about all the plastic waste. I saw this documentary on PBS the other night about the ocean garbage patches. Just massive islands of plastic floating out there. They had this footage of a sea turtle that was all tangled up in a soda ring... really makes you think about recycling. We've been trying to be better about it, putting the bins out on Thursday nights. Our garbage man, Sal, he's a great guy. Always waves when he drives by...

Wait, I think I already told you about the office stuff, didn't I? Did you ask about interrupting again?
At home or in social situations, do you often blurt things out or cut people off before they finish speaking?

I feel like we just covered this, doc, but yeah, at home it's not a huge thing. Maybe with my wife now and then. It's really the office where it happens. I don't mean to be rude, but if I hear the coworkers next to me trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump in with the answer before they've even finished talking, or before anyone even asked me. 

I mean, I know the system inside and out. Even though it's practically from the Stone Age. I keep telling management we need an upgrade. The software freezes up if you look at it wrong. Last week, I lost a whole customer file because the screen just went black. I had to call IT, and they sent over this guy, Kevin. Kevin's a nice kid, but he talks so slow. Like, painfully slow. He was trying to explain to me how to clear my cache, and I just wanted to grab the mouse and do it myself. He was wearing this band t-shirt, some heavy metal group I'd never heard of. My son used to listen to that kind of music when he was in high school. The drums were always so loud, shaking the whole house. He played the drums himself for a while. We set up a kit in the garage, but the neighbors complained about the noise. Old Mrs. Higgins next door, she had this little poodle that would just howl every time he hit the snare drum. That dog was something else. Used to dig under the fence and ruin my wife's petunias...

Wait, did you ask about blurting things out again? I swear my brain is just jumping all over the place today.
Outside of work, do you also have trouble paying attention when you’re trying to focus?

Outside of work? No, not really. I don't read much at home anyway, mostly just watch TV. But at work, yeah, that's where I really notice it. Like when we have those longer coaching meetings, or if they hand me a manual for a new procedure. I'll start off fine, you know, reading along. But after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page and I haven't actually taken in a single word of what I just read. 

It's kind of like when I try to read the instruction manuals for the stuff my wife buys at IKEA. She loves that place. The meatballs in the cafeteria are pretty good, I have to admit, but putting the furniture together? It's a nightmare. The pictures never make sense. We bought this bookshelf last month, the "Billy" or something they called it. Took me three hours and I still had parts left over. I ended up just using wood glue to hold the top shelf on. It's holding up okay so far, but she's got all her heavy gardening books on it, so I'm just waiting for the day it collapses. She's really gotten into gardening lately. Tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers. We had so many cucumbers last summer we didn't know what to do with them. I tried making pickles, but I used the wrong kind of vinegar and they tasted awful. My neighbor, Gary, he makes his own beer in his garage. He gave me a bottle of his IPA once... man, it was bitter. I don't know how people drink that stuff. I'm more of a classic lager guy myself. Just a simple, cold beer after a long day of dealing with angry customers on the phone...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, trouble paying attention outside of work? Yeah, like I said, not so much at home, mostly just at the office with the reading and the meetings.
Outside of work, do you often feel restless or find yourself fidgeting?

Outside of work? Restless? Honestly, not really. Once I'm home, I usually just crash in my recliner. It's the one we got from that big furniture blowout sale last Labor Day. It's got this built-in massage feature, which sounds great, but it really just vibrates aggressively. Rattles my teeth if I turn it up past level two. My wife hates it because it makes this loud humming noise that she says interferes with her shows. She's been watching those British baking competitions non-stop. I don't get the appeal, honestly. They get so worked up over a soggy bottom on a pie crust. But I guess everyone has their thing. 

But, uh, where was I? Oh, the restless thing. Yeah, it's mostly at the office. Even when I'm trying to look totally calm and professional, my foot is just bouncing away under the desk. Or I'll be in one of those endless staff meetings, and I'll realize I've been clicking my pen open and closed for ten minutes straight without even noticing. It drives the guy next to me crazy. He's one of those guys who has his whole desk organized perfectly, little trays for everything. He even has a tiny vacuum for his keyboard. I saw it on Amazon once, thought about getting one for my car. The floorboards are covered in cracker crumbs from when the grandkids were over last weekend. They're good kids, but man, they leave a trail of destruction wherever they go. The youngest, little Timmy, he managed to get peanut butter on the ceiling somehow. Still haven't figured that one out. 

Wait, did you ask about my grandkids or the fidgeting? I think I got off track again.
Outside of work, do you also interrupt people before they finish speaking?

I feel like I'm having a serious case of deja vu here, doc. Didn't we just talk about this? But no, outside of work, not really. It's not a huge thing at home. Maybe I'll cut my wife off now and then, but she usually just tells me to hush. It's really just the office where it happens. Like I was saying before, I don't mean to be rude, but if I hear the coworkers next to me trying to work through a customer problem, I'll just jump in with the answer before they've even finished talking, or before anyone even asked me. 

I just know the system so well, you know? It's second nature at this point. Even if the system itself is a dinosaur. I swear, the computers we use must be from the 90s. They still have those clunky beige monitors. My grandson asked me if it was a TV the other day when I showed him a picture of my desk. He's obsessed with electronics. Always on his tablet, playing those games where you build things out of blocks. Minecraft, I think it's called. He tried to teach me how to play once, but I couldn't get the hang of it. I kept digging straight down and falling into lava. He thought it was the funniest thing in the world. Kids these days, they're born knowing how to use touchscreens. When I was his age, the most advanced piece of technology we had in the house was a rotary phone. And it was attached to the wall! You couldn't just walk around the house talking to people. You had to stand right there in the kitchen, usually with my mother eavesdropping while she washed the dishes. She made the best pot roast, though. Slow-cooked all day with carrots and potatoes...

Wait, did you ask about the interrupting thing again? Yeah, like I said, mostly just at the office with the customer problems.
Outside of work, do you often have trouble staying seated when you’re expected to remain seated?

Not really, no. I mean, at home I'm pretty good at staying put. Usually I'm just in my recliner, like I mentioned. Or I'm out in the garage. I like tinkering out there. Just messing around with my tools. I've got this old workbench my dad built. It's solid oak, weighs a ton. He used to fix everything on that bench. Lawnmowers, radios, you name it. He even tried to fix my mom's sewing machine once, but he ended up with a bunch of extra springs and gears and she had to take it to a professional anyway. She was so mad. She used to make all our clothes when we were little. I had this one pair of corduroy pants she made... bright orange. I hated those pants. Every time I walked, my thighs would rub together and make this loud swishing sound. Swish, swish, swish down the hallway at school. The other kids never let me hear the end of it. Kids can be really cruel, you know? My grandson, the one who likes the video games, he was telling me about some kid at school who was picking on him because of his shoes. Can you believe that? Shoes! Back in my day, you wore whatever sneakers your parents bought you until the soles fell off. And you liked it! We used to play stickball out in the street until the streetlights came on...

Anyway, what was I talking about? Oh, staying seated. Yeah, at home it's not a problem. Work is a different story, though. Like I've said, I can't sit still at my desk for very long. I'm always popping up to go to the water cooler, or the bathroom, or just to walk over and ask a question I probably could have just sent in an email.
Do you often lose things you need for work or other daily activities?

Lose things? No, not really. I'm actually pretty good about keeping track of my stuff. I mean, my desk at work is a little cluttered, sure, but I know where everything is. It's organized chaos, as they say. Like, my wife, she's the one who loses things. She's always misplacing her reading glasses. She'll buy a three-pack from the drugstore and lose them all within a week. I tell her she needs to get one of those little chains to hang them around her neck, like the librarians used to wear. We had this librarian when I was in high school, Mrs. Gable. She was terrifying. Had this huge beehive hairdo that looked like it was sprayed with concrete. You could smell the Aqua Net from three aisles over. She caught me and my buddy Steve trying to sneak a comic book inside a history encyclopedia once. Steve was a real character. He ended up moving to Florida to open a bait shop. Always said he wanted to live somewhere he didn't have to shovel snow. I don't blame him. Last winter, my snowblower broke on the first big storm of the year. Had to shovel the whole driveway by hand. My back was killing me for a week. I had to use this heating pad that smelled vaguely of wet dog... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, losing things. Yeah, no, I usually know exactly where my keys and wallet are. I'm pretty good about that.
Outside of work, do you also have trouble paying attention during conversations?

Outside of work? No, not really. I can chat with my wife or the guys at the hardware store just fine. It's really just a work thing. Like, when we have those long coaching meetings, or if I have to read through a new procedure... I'll start off fine, you know? But then after a few minutes, I'll realize my eyes have just been moving across the page and I didn't actually take in a single word. Or I'll be sitting there in the meeting and suddenly realize I haven't heard the last five minutes of what my supervisor was saying. 

My supervisor, Greg, he's a nice enough guy, but he has this voice that just drones on. It's like a lawnmower running three houses down. Just this constant hum. He wears these awful ties, too. Yesterday he had one on that looked like a bowl of fruit exploded. I don't know where he shops. Probably the same place my brother-in-law gets his shirts. My brother-in-law, Dave, he loves these loud Hawaiian shirts. Even in the dead of winter! We had him over for Christmas dinner last year and he showed up in a shirt with hula dancers all over it. My wife was mortified, but I thought it was hilarious. We had a good laugh about it later. We always do a big ham for Christmas, with pineapple rings on top. The secret is brown sugar and a little bit of mustard in the glaze. My mother taught me that trick...

But yeah, anyway, the attention thing. Just at work, mostly during those long meetings or when I'm trying to read through all that boring new policy stuff they send out.
At home, do you often have trouble finishing chores because your mind wanders or you get distracted?

Chores at home? No, my wife usually handles most of the inside stuff, and I do the yard work. I don't really have a problem finishing mowing the lawn or anything. But, you know, it's funny you mention getting distracted and not finishing things, because that happens to me at work all the time. 

Like, if a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation... I'll usually do the first part right away. But then somehow I'll just leave the notes or the follow-up sitting there unfinished until someone reminds me. It's like it just vanishes from my brain. I don't know why that happens. My buddy Steve, the one in Florida with the bait shop? He used to say his brain was like a sieve. He'd go to the store for milk and come back with a six-pack of beer and a bag of charcoal, and completely forget the milk. We used to grill out all the time before he moved. He made the best ribs. He had this dry rub recipe he wouldn't share with anyone. Said he'd take it to his grave. I tried to recreate it a few times, but it just wasn't the same. I think the secret was smoked paprika, but I could never get the ratio right. I bought this huge container of it from one of those warehouse clubs, and it's just been sitting in my pantry for three years. Those warehouse clubs are dangerous, you know? You go in for paper towels and come out with a kayak and a 50-pound bag of rice... 

But yeah, anyway, the unfinished stuff. Not so much at home with chores, but definitely at work with those escalations. I just kind of drop the ball on the follow-up part.

doctor.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking care today
doctor.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

target_item.name: Constant_Activity
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that I feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, like I can’t just idle, and the new work setup has made that a lot harder to hide.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code, which is S014.

patient.answer:
Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just feel like I’m always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I can't ever just idle. And the new work setup has made that a lot harder to hide. 

They just moved all of us customer service reps to this new open-floor plan. Which, honestly, is a terrible idea. I mean, you've got fifty people all talking on headsets at once, and the headsets they gave us are those cheap foam ones? My ear actually gets a rash if I wear it for more than an hour. My wife told me to put a little baby powder on it, but that just gets all over my shirt collar, and then it looks like I've been eating powdered donuts all morning. I complained to HR about the headsets, but they said it's standard issue now. 

But anyway... yeah, I just can't idle, and with the new desks, everyone can see it now.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a distinct manic or hypomanic episode, which would separate bipolar disorder from ADHD or anxiety.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when your mood was unusually high or irritable compared with your normal self?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about periods of unusually high or irritable mood, which relates to symptoms of mania or hypomania (bipolar disorder). None of the symptom profiles provided cover mood symptoms, mania, or irritability.

patient.answer:
Unusually high? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I don't get super high or anything. I get irritated, sure, but just the normal amount, you know? 

Like, when someone leaves the breakroom microwave covered in whatever they just heated up. Yesterday it looked like a literal tomato soup explosion in there. Who just leaves that? It’s a shared space. And don't even get me started on the coffee machine. Management switched us to this cheap brand to save a few bucks, and it tastes like burnt dirt. My wife tells me I should just bring a thermos from home, but by the time I get through the morning traffic on the interstate—which is a total nightmare right now because of that construction they're doing on the overpass—the coffee is lukewarm anyway. I even bought one of those fancy insulated travel mugs, but the seal on the lid is defective or something because it always leaks right onto my car seats. Yesterday he had one on that looked like a bowl of fruit exploded. I don't know where he shops. Probably the same place my brother-in-law gets his shirts. My brother-in-law, Dave, he loves these loud Hawaiian shirts. Even in the dead of winter! We had him over for Christmas dinner last year and he showed up in a shirt with hula dancers all over it. My wife was mortified, but I thought it was hilarious. We had a good laugh about it later. We always do a big ham for Christmas, with pineapple rings on top. The secret is brown sugar and a little bit of mustard in the glaze. My mother taught me that trick...

But yeah, anyway, the attention thing. Just at work, mostly during those long meetings or when I'm trying to read through all that boring new policy stuff they send out.

doctor.intent: Determine whether inattentive symptoms occur across settings outside of work, which best distinguishes predominantly inattentive type from combined type given the patient’s mostly work-specific hyperactive/impulsive symptoms.
doctor.question: At home, do you often have trouble finishing chores because your mind wanders or you get distracted?

target_item.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
target_item.manifestation: If a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation, I usually do the first part and then somehow leave the notes or follow-up sitting there unfinished until someone reminds me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about having trouble finishing chores, which directly corresponds to the symptom of failing to follow through and finish chores or duties.

patient.answer:
Chores at home? No, my wife usually handles most of the inside stuff, and I do the yard work. I don't really have a problem finishing mowing the lawn or anything. But, you know, it's funny you mention getting distracted and not finishing things, because that happens to me at work all the time. 

Like, if a supervisor gives me three or four steps for a chat escalation... I'll usually do the first part right away. But then somehow I'll just leave the notes or the follow-up sitting there unfinished until someone reminds me. It's like it just vanishes from my brain. I don't know why that happens. My buddy Steve, the one in Florida with the bait shop? He used to say his brain was like a sieve. He'd go to the store for milk and come back with a six-pack of beer and a bag of charcoal, and completely forget the milk. We used to grill out all the time before he moved. He made the best ribs. He had this dry rub recipe he wouldn't share with anyone. Said he'd take it to his grave. I tried to recreate it a few times, but it just wasn't the same. I think the secret was smoked paprika, but I could never get the ratio right. I bought this huge container of it from one of those warehouse clubs, and it's just been sitting in my pantry for three years. Those warehouse clubs are dangerous, you know? You go in for paper towels and come out with a kayak and a 50-pound bag of rice... 

But yeah, anyway, the unfinished stuff. Not so much at home with chores, but definitely at work with those escalations. I just kind of drop the ball on the follow-up part.

opening_question.question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient shows clear ADHD symptoms with both inattentive and hyperactive/restless features beginning in childhood and causing occupational impairment, but the interview does not establish the broader cross-situational hyperactive/impulsive pattern needed for combined presentation. Symptoms are reported predominantly at work, while home/social hyperactivity and impulsivity are mostly denied. Thus the best fit among the offered choices is disturbance of activity and attention.
